fieldMarks: Cat-sized with a stout body, small head, short legs and a long-haired bushy tail; 20-30 in long.
Black fur with a thin white stripe down the face and a broad white stripe from the head that forks at the shoulders into two back stripes.
Stripe pattern varies individually, from nearly absent to covering the whole back.
behavior: Mostly nocturnal forager; omnivorous, favouring insects (including bee and wasp larvae) in spring and summer, plus mice, other small mammals and carrion.
Warns before spraying by stamping its front feet, raising its tail, growling or hissing; often smelled before seen.
Usually dens in abandoned burrows of woodchucks or foxes, or under stumps, rock piles and buildings.
habitat: Mixed farmland, forest edges, brushy field corners, fencerows and grassy fields broken by wooded ravines, near permanent water; adapts well to people.
range: From central Mexico north to the Northwest Territories and Nunavut, and from the Maritimes to west-central British Columbia, across the United States.

lookalikes.name: Spotted skunks
lookalikes.howToTell: Spotted skunks are much smaller and marked with several broken white stripes and spots, including a white forehead spot.
